44	- **A RING AND A DIGIT THAT SHARE ONE TOKEN FUSE INTO ONE READING (R116, load-bearing).** R115 read our selection as a ring peaking `(0,136,255)` with the digit `(63,63,66)`, "32 px, the cell's modal non-plane tone". The deleted source shows why that is a **two-tone misidentification**: the digit's colour *was* `root.tahoe.accent`, i.e. **the same `(0,136,255)` as the border**, and the tone it took for the digit is dark `selectionFill` (`0x76,0x76,0x80 @30%` over the 40 plane) = **63** — the **ring's interior fill**. ⇒ **Before calling a value "the digit", check the source for the digit's colour and the outline's colour: if they are one token, a threshold ladder cannot separate them and a ×6 zoom still cannot.** (Inference from the removed code, not a re-measurement.)
45	- **THE MINI MONTH'S GRID IS MONTH-INDEPENDENT (R115, load-bearing).** The six date-band tops are **561/582/603/624/645/666** — identical in the Apr-2026 capture (R112/R114) and the Oct-2026 one (R115/R116) — and the disc overhangs its 9-row band by **4 above / 2 below** in all of them. A mini-month reading taken on one month therefore holds for any month.
46	- **A 9-ROW GLYPH INSIDE A 15 px RING IS NOT LEGIBLE ENOUGH TO CARRY A TONE CLAIM (R115, load-bearing).** R112/R114 read the selection disc's digit as "the ordinary text tone" at 1:1; the **×6 zoom** separated a 63-tone fill from a 216-tone glyph. **Ring/disc interiors need a zoom before any tone claim** — a threshold that separates the ring from the plane will not separate the digit from the ring. **(R116: the digit and the ring were one token, so even the zoom needed the source. See the bullet above.)**
47	- **THE CLAUSE AND THE REFERENCE CAN DISAGREE ON A SIZE (R115, load-bearing).** M04 says the today circle is **18–20**; the ref's is **15 at 1:1** and **17.3** in our layout (scale 1.155, derived two ways). **When a spec literal is not the reference at any measurable scale, the literal wins by default but the ref numbers must be recorded beside it** — the ruling is not ours to make. **R116: this is why (b) is 18 and not 15.**
48	- **THE SIDEBAR'S 1 px RIM AT x220 EXISTS ON BOTH LEGS (R114, load-bearing).** Dark `(53,53,53)` at x220 with the plane 40 at x219; light `(224,224,224)` with the plane 228. **A whole-sidebar ink scan must stop at x219:** over x0..**220** the dark leg returns a single band (490,691) because every row contains the rim, while the light leg's rim is only 4 tones off the plane and hides under a threshold of 8. **A whole-sidebar test that passes on light can be silently vacuous on dark — always name the x range and check the rim.**
49	- **THE MINI MONTH HAS NO FILL OF ITS OWN (R114, load-bearing).** The block's field IS the sidebar plane ((40,40,40) dark / 228 light, the dominant tone in **every** row of the block), so **M01's 12 / 12 margins are arithmetic, not tonal**: they follow from `cellWidth 196/7 = 28.0` and the column centres 26.0 + 28.0i (=> cells 12..208 in a 220 px sidebar) and can never be read off a fill edge. The same is true on light. **R116 re-witnessed: the disc row's scan is dominated by the 228 plane (467 px of 660 in the selection cell).**
50	- **A BAND SCAN ON A DISC-BEARING ROW MUST BE DISC-FREE (R114).** The 15x15 selection disc extends **4 px above and 2 px below** the 9-row text band, so a full-width scan of the selected row reads wider than a disc-free scan (R112's clean six 9-row bands). The disc is **15x15 on both legs**; its ring is blue (dark peak `(0,136,255)`, light ~`(39,152,250)`) — **superseded by R116: the disc is now gray `(142,142,147)` with no ring; the 4-above/2-below overhang is unchanged.** **It never appears in the Apr-2026 fixture's today state, because today is not in that week.**
51	- **THE PAIR, NOT THE BOX, IS THE INSTRUMENT ON A DARK LEG (R114).** An ink box reads ±1 px differently against a 40 plane than against 228 (dark `x24..27 / y523..527` vs light/R112 `x24..28 / y523..528` for the SAME glyph at two thresholds). So a dark-leg fidelity claim must rest on a **pair comparison** — arrow vs arrow, dark vs light, at two thresholds — and never on an absolute box edge. **R116 used the same instrument on one leg: the two discs measure equal to the pixel (102..116 vs 158..172, same y599..613).**
52	- **A PIXEL RUN p..q IS THE HALF-OPEN INTERVAL [p, q+1) — ITS CENTRE IS (p+q+1)/2 (R112, load-bearing calibration).** The inclusive form `(p+q)/2` shifts every centre 0.5 px left; on the mini month it produced margins **11.5 / 12.5** where the layout can only have equal ones (`Main.qml:2122-2123` sets the *same* `categoryInset` on both sides). The source broke the tie, and the half-open form then reproduced `categoryInset` = **12 / 12** exactly. **Corollary (the project's own R066/R111 convention): a GAP written as `line - last_ink_pixel` ("ink 44, line 52 => gap 8") is the inclusive form and reads 1 larger than the continuous gap.** Mixing the two forms is a 1 px error — so state which form a gap came from.
53	- **A DARK `gridLine` COMPOSITES, A LIGHT ONE DOES NOT (R113, load-bearing).** The dark separators read **59** over the weekday field 30 and **65** over the weekend tint 37 — one token, `white@0.13`, two backdrops. The light `#EDEDED` is opaque and reads 237 everywhere. => **"all separators share one tone" is a light-leg fact; a dark scan must expect two, and a differing separator tone is not a separator-tone bug until the backdrop under it is checked.**
54	- **A RULE ROW'S GUTTER SEGMENT IS THE LABEL, NEVER A LINE (R111, load-bearing).** The hour/half-hour rules span **x272..x1099** only — the grid's left edge to the window's last pixel. In a rule row the only non-white pixels left of x272 are the gutter label's own ink (`238..264`). => **"does the rule reach across the gutter?" must be scanned right of the label ink, never by a whole-row `!= white` test.**
55	- **A CLIPPED LABEL BAND IS STILL AN ALIGNMENT READING IF ITS INK X-EXTENT MATCHES ITS SIBLINGS (R111).** The topmost visible label is clipped by the scroll viewport (visible 234..238 of a 230..238 band), so its visible-band *centre* reads 2 px late. Judge alignment on unclipped bands, or on the clipped band's **identical ink x-extent**.
56	- **THE HOUR LABELS SCROLL WITH THE GRID (R111, load-bearing).** At `contentY 240` (= 6x40) the top tick is hour 6 at screen y234 and the label bands sit at 274/314/.../674 — a gutter scan must be indexed by **tick**, not by absolute hour. The y-map **above** the grid (155 / 156..231 / 232-233 / 234) is fixed and does not scroll; only the grid's own rules and labels move.
57	- **EXPANDED-SIDEBAR T03 GEOMETRY, MEASURED (R111).** Gutter **221..272**; label ink **x238..264**, right gap **8** to the grid line at 272 — the same 8 as the collapsed leg's R066 reading (ink 44, line 52). Separators **1 px 237** at **272/391/510/629/748/867** (**pitch 119**); weekend tint **249** right of the x867 separator. Label band = **9 rows**, font 11.
58	- **AN OPAQUE PRE-BLEND MUST RESOLVE THE WEEKEND TINT FIRST (R109, load-bearing).** `weekendField`'s dark leg is `white@0.03` — **translucent** — so feeding it to `mix()`/`withAlpha()` drops its alpha and the blend starts from the untinted field. `allDayBackdrop()` composites it explicitly: dark ⇒ `mix(field, white, 0.03)` ≈ **37**; light `#F9F9F9` is already opaque so it passes through. R110 read the weekend FIELD on dark: pure `(37,37,37)` at (1000,300) and (900,600) — the composite resolves to the documented 37. **The weekend CHIP is still UNWITNESSED — the fixture's Sat/Sun all-day columns are empty (R107).** Never claim a weekend chip backdrop was read.
59	- **`opacity: 0.5` ON A COMPLETED ITEM RE-CREATES THE EXACT DEFECT R109 FIXED (R109, load-bearing).** `CalendarScheduleView.qml:550` still fades a completed chip with item `opacity`, which composites the chip against what is *below* it — two overlapping 50 % chips would stack darker than the bar, exactly as R108's translucent overlap did. **No completed all-day item exists in the fixture. Recorded, not fixed.**
60	- **A TRANSLUCENT CHIP CANNOT BE JOINED BY OVERLAP (R108, load-bearing).** `withAlpha(itemColor, 0.17)` over white is **220** and two overlapping chips stack to **191** — 11 % darker. **A join must be an opaque pre-blend (R109's `AppTheme.mix(backdrop, itemColor, a)`), after which the extension can be generous and immune to the ±1 rounding.** R109 is the confirmation: reach = 3 px measured, 4 px shipped.
61	- **THE JOINT'S 3 px IS ONE PIXEL OF SLACK IN THREE PIECES (R108, load-bearing).** A column is **119.0 px** (833/7) and draws its own 1 px separator as its **FIRST** pixel; the chips sit in a `ColumnLayout` inset `allDayBandInset: 1` ⇒ a chip is **116 px inside a 119 px column**. Joint = 2 px field (column leftover + layout rounding) + the neighbour's separator + the neighbour's own 1 px inset. **The leftover is known only to ±1 — that is what disqualifies an exact-fit margin and makes an overlapping one necessary.**
62	- **ONLY A LEFT-EXTENSION CAN HIDE A RULE (R108, load-bearing).** Each column's separator belongs to **that column's own delegate**, which is later in the RowLayout than the previous column's chips ⇒ it paints **above** them. So a right-extension can never cover the neighbour's rule; the neighbour's own chip, extending **left**, can. **R109 shipped exactly that: `Layout.leftMargin` only, never a right one.**
63	- **A CONTINUATION IS A DATE FACT; A COLUMN IS A PLACE (R109, load-bearing).** `allDayContinues()` (`:243-252`) is pure date arithmetic, so it returns `true` on column 0 for an item that started in the *previous week* — with a reach attached that would paint 4 px into the gutter with no rounding column. **Gate the reach on `allDayColumn.index > 0`.** The corner suppression (clause (a)) still reads the ungated flag.
64	- **THE ALL-DAY BAND IS CONTENT-SIZED WITH A ONE-ROW FLOOR (R106, load-bearing).** `allDayBandRows = clamp(maxItemsAcrossThe7Columns, 1, 3)`: **26 px** all-day-empty, **76** on the 3-row week. **`allDayMaxRows` (the cap, 3) and `allDayBandRows` (the drawn rows) must stay separate variables.**
65	- **OUR WEEKS START MONDAY, AND AN EXPANDED SIDEBAR SHIFTS THE DAY COLUMNS (R106, load-bearing).** With the sidebar expanded the gutter runs **221..272** and the separators sit at **272/391/510/629/748/867/986** — **pitch 119**. So **`x=577` is the 3rd day column; Thursday is 629..747 (x~690)**. The y-map is x-independent; only *horizontal* reads need the leg's sidebar state stated. **R115/R116 note: the reference's mini month headers read `S M T W T F S` (Sunday-first) where ours read `一二三四五六日` (Monday-first) — an unfiled heading/header divergence, recorded on the dark leg. M02's seven-equal-columns and six-equal-rows clauses are unaffected.**
66	- **AN ALL-DAY-EMPTY WEEK STILL SHOWS A 26 px BAND (R106, extrapolation).** The spec says "min about 28", so the band has a floor rather than a hide.
67	- **THE REF'S SIDEBAR IS 192 px WIDE — "243px sidebar" WAS A CONFLATION (R105, load-bearing).** The 237-plane ends at **x=191**; the white hour gutter runs **192..243** and the first *day column* starts at **243**. ⇒ the reference's **main region is 192..813, centre 502.5** — and its segment's rim centre is **502.0**. **R063–R104 carried the wrong denominator ⇒ any ref-centredness number derived from "grid 243..812" must be recomputed.**
68	- **A CENTRED-IN-REGION SEGMENT IS −0.5 px ON BOTH SIDES, AND THAT IS THE CONVENTION (R105, load-bearing).**
69	- **A CAPSULE'S OUTER RADIUS IS MEASURED AGAINST ITS OWN INNER ELEMENT, NEVER IN ABSOLUTE PX (R104, load-bearing).**
70	- **AN ARC-ONLY FIT CANNOT SEPARATE r FROM y0 AND IS THEREFORE NOT AN ABSOLUTE INSTRUMENT (R104, load-bearing).** **Report the bound (11–13.5), not a point.**
71	- **A PILL'S HORIZONTAL PADDING IS MEASURED AGAINST ITS OWN SLOT, AND THE SLOTS OF A SEGMENTED CONTROL TILE (R102, load-bearing; R103).** **R103: the rule applies to both sides or the comparison is void. Correct ref slot = (228−4)/4 = 56.0.**
72	- **A WHOLE-CONTROL WIDTH CAN BE A SPEC LITERAL THAT OVERRIDES THE REFERENCE (R103, load-bearing).** **L03 fixes 180–210 ⇒ a 3-label control can never match a 4-label reference's pill width.**
73	- **WORD CENTRES BEAT CONTROL EDGES FOR A PITCH (R103, load-bearing).**
74	- **THE REFERENCE'S SEGMENTED CONTROL AND OURS SHARE ONE RADIUS TOKEN (R101–R104).** Ref lens **r ≈ 11.5 on h 24 (0.48)**; ref track **r ≈ 13.4–13.5**; ours **0.48 on both**.
75	- **A RADIUS IS MEASURED 1:1 AGAINST A SAME-HEIGHT ELEMENT, AND THE METHOD MUST RECOVER A KNOWN TOKEN FIRST (R101, load-bearing).** **threshold = the midpoint of THAT IMAGE's own two constants**; **only when the profile is monotone across the edge. R104: prefer the *within-image* track-vs-lens profile.**
76	- **A WHOLE-PAGE `ImageChops.difference` WITH A PER-ROW DIFF COUNT IS STILL THE CHEAPEST CONTAINMENT PROOF (R088).** Threshold **>6 RGB-sum**. **R109 used it to prove the `index > 0` guard is invisible: two captures differ by max 1/255 across the whole page.**
77	- **NEVER SCALE A REF *TYPE* ELEMENT BY THE WINDOW RATIO — FIND A SAME-CLASS INK IN BOTH IMAGES FIRST (R086).**
78	- **MEASURING A CORNER, A JOINT, A STRIPE, A BORDER OR AN INK (R075–R116).** Corner: per-row **fill-start inset** (body mode, R098; **interior rows, indexed from the first counted row, validated on a known token — R101/R102**; **R103: only on a monotone edge**; **R104: on a 250-on-255 fill use the rim's argmin core, and compare the outer element against the inner one in the SAME image**). Joint: per-row **`!= white` envelope**; **R107: a shared *horizontal* edge is separator-tone + the very next row's tone; R108: a shared *vertical* edge is the pair of fill edges plus whatever sits between them, and a JOIN must be read as an absolute tone against the fill (a translucent overlap reads DARKER, not lighter); R109: after the join, the acceptance is "the fill envelope is unbroken and contains no 255 and no rule tone".** Stripe: a saturated run whose **width is constant over the chip's full height**. Border: **monotonicity of a raw profile across an edge that abuts no rule**. Ink: the **per-channel coverage agreement test PLUS the channel-gap argument**; cross-capture: **top-5 %-coverage mean** and **`n<100`**; **R115: a glyph inside a disc/ring needs a ×6 zoom — thresholding the disc out of the plane does not threshold the digit out of the disc**; **R116: and if the glyph and its outline share one token, even the zoom needs the source — report the *fill* tone and the *outline* tone separately, and say which one you called the glyph.** **Pitch: word centres, not edges (R103).**
79	- **HARNESS / COMMAND / TOKEN RULES.**
80	  **`captureClient` RETURNS `false` ON A NESTED RELATIVE PATH AND THE PNG IS SILENTLY NOT WRITTEN (R075).** Pass a **flat filename**; read the success flag in `live-runtime-vm.log`, then `ls` the actual CWD. **Pillow crops need ABSOLUTE paths** — the shell CWD moves between calls. **R107: our PNGs are written at zlib level 0 — three different captures share a byte size, so compare `md5sum`, never the size.**
81	  **THE LAUNCHER REFUSES WHEN A LIVED INSTANCE IS ALIVE (R079), AND `>/dev/null` HIDES IT.** `start-review-vm.sh` exits **1** with `Owned review instance still running: <pid>`. **ALWAYS `kill -0 $(cat live-app.pid)` FIRST: if the leg you need is already alive, the capture is FREE** (R114/R115 both took that path and touched nothing). **R116: a REBUILT binary needs kill + relaunch — a live instance keeps running the OLD resources, theme fixed at launch — so a source change always costs the full cycle (kill `live-app.pid` → `nohup ./start-review-vm.sh light|dark &` → `sleep 40` → `python3 review-command.py '<json list>'` → grep `capture <name>.png true`).**
82	  **`review-command.py` IS NOT EXECUTABLE — always `python3 review-command.py`.** It is ~15 lines: it takes **ONE argv that is a JSON list**, bumps `sequence` from the file's own last value, writes **in place** (never `os.replace`), sleeps 0.6 s between commands.
83	  **HARNESS COMMAND FORM IS FLAT (R064).** `harness/Main.qml` matches `command.action` only; a command with no `action` **silently hits the fallback**.
